predictions.title: Big-3 hyperscalers publish AI-services 10-Q revenue footnote by Q1 2027
predictions.body: By Q1 2027 the May 7 Mag-7 disclosure cohort tightening — Microsoft's post-earnings analyst-day disclosure of an Azure AI Services run-rate now at $52B annualized (vs $38B prior quarter) with CFO Amy Hood guiding to a Q4 "AI Services" 10-Q footnote breakout starting fiscal Q1-2027, Apple printing services revenue $28.4B (+14% YoY) with Apple Intelligence + Foundry Local cited as margin-accretive, Alphabet announcing $9B incremental capex for the Iowa Gemini training cluster (2026 capex guide $94B), and Meta's Llama 4 Maverick + Behemoth roadmap targeting frontier-cyber parity with Mythos by Q4 2026 — combined with the Cerebras IPO above-range pricing print that puts a public-market multiple under disclosed AI-accelerator revenue, force Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta to publish parallel AI-services revenue 10-Q footnote breakouts inside the same fiscal cycle. The structural force is that once one Mag-7 issuer ships a mid-2-digit-billions AI-segment disclosure with a committed footnote-breakout schedule, sell-side and SEC Corp Fin staff comment letters press the cohort for comparable line items; the AI-capex-vs-AI-revenue ROI question that Mag-7 Q1 prints left unresolved becomes politically untenable to leave to analyst-day commentary alone. The most likely shape is a quantitative AI Services revenue line + segment-level cost-of-revenue + capex-to-AI-services attribution narrative; Alphabet ships first given its $9B incremental Iowa capex needing an ROI denominator, Amazon follows on the AWS Bedrock + Trainium footnote, Meta last given its open-weights commercial model. The bear case is SEC Corp Fin issuing a concept release first and delaying voluntary disclosure beyond Q1 2027; absent that, the cohort lands by fiscal Q1-2027 prints.

reasoning.because: Microsoft May 7 analyst day discloses $52B Azure AI Services run-rate + Q1-2027 footnote commitment.
reasoning.given: Cerebras IPO public-market multiple + unresolved Mag-7 AI-capex-vs-revenue ROI gap pressure cohort.
reasoning.so_that: Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta publish parallel AI-services revenue 10-Q footnote breakouts inside the same fiscal cycle.
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; Alphabet first on $9B Iowa capex ROI denominator pressure.
reasoning.plain_language: Microsoft promised to break out its AI sales line in its next big report, so Google, Amazon, and Meta will copy.

predictions.summary: Microsoft's May 7 disclosure of $52B annualized Azure AI Services run-rate plus a committed Q1-2027 10-Q footnote breakout, paired with the Cerebras IPO public-market multiple, forces the cohort to follow. By Q1 2027 Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta publish parallel AI-services revenue 10-Q footnotes.

predictions.title: Frontier-lab chip-supply warrant deals enter S-1 disclosure standard by Q1 2027
predictions.body: By Q1 2027 the May 6-7 Cerebras Systems IPO above-range pricing print — $128 per share (vs $115-$125 disclosed range, +2.4% above the upper end), $3.58B raise lifted to ~$4.12B with the green-shoe exercised in full at a fully-diluted ~$27.2B market cap, OpenAI's December 2025 $1B warrant package (~33M shares, ~12% of float, struck at the Series H reference) marked publicly in-the-money on listing day, Sam Altman + Greg Brockman + Ilya Sutskever + Adam D'Angelo angel positions all crystallized at a $26.6B-target → $27.2B-actual print — combined with the May 7 SambaNova + Groq accelerated S-1 confidential-submission timelines (60-90 days), the Tenstorrent Hyundai + Samsung Foundry IPO bridge round at >$3B, and a public-market multiple now sitting under disclosed AI-accelerator revenue, force the next wave of S-1 filings (and existing AI-accelerator + frontier-lab 10-Q footnote schedules) to disclose frontier-lab chip-supply warrant and loan terms as a standard issuer-level itemized exhibit rather than buried among related-party narrative footnotes. The forcing function is that OpenAI's Cerebras warrant is the first publicly-priced data point linking a frontier lab's structured-equity supply contract to an open-market multiple; sell-side and SEC Corp Fin staff comment letters now have a quantitative comparable to press for, which converts what was bespoke disclosure into template language. The most likely shape is an itemized warrant-and-loan exhibit naming counterparty (frontier lab), strike reference (Series-letter peg), share count, coverage clause, and any minimum-revenue or capacity-take obligations; SambaNova's S-1 ships first given its ~$5.1B last-priced round and Aramco Digital + Meta API customer roster, Groq second on its Saudi-anchored vehicle and inference-tier API revenue, Tenstorrent third via its bridge-round disclosure. Bear case is that the SEC permits silence on coverage clauses pending a separate concept release; absent that, Q1 2027 lands the standardised exhibit shape across the cohort.

reasoning.because: Cerebras IPO pricing puts OpenAI's $1B warrant package publicly in-the-money on listing day May 7.
reasoning.given: SambaNova + Groq + Tenstorrent S-1 prep gives frontier-lab supply contracts a public comparable.
reasoning.so_that: S-1 and 10-Q filings disclose frontier-lab chip-supply warrant and loan terms as standard itemized exhibits.
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; SambaNova S-1 first, Groq second, Tenstorrent third on bridge round.
reasoning.plain_language: Cerebras went public and OpenAI's warrant deal showed up on its books, so future chip-startup IPOs will spell out their frontier-lab contract terms.

predictions.summary: Cerebras's May 7 above-range IPO marks OpenAI's $1B warrant publicly in-the-money and gives sell-side a direct comparable for frontier-lab supply contracts. By Q1 2027 SambaNova, Groq, and Tenstorrent S-1s disclose chip-supply warrant and loan terms as a standard itemized exhibit.

predictions.title: Signed agent-skill registries land as enterprise procurement default by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the May 7 dual-registry landing — Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 shipping a sandboxed-skill registry that signs and version-pins shareable agent skills with per-tenant Mythos Preview gating tied to AISI cyber-eval results (Project Glasswing extension), and OpenAI graduating the May-1 Codex CLI /goal feature into a /agent command with explicit Plan-Apply two-phase execution alongside ChatGPT Enterprise's per-org agent registry GA with FedRAMP-Moderate authorization + SOC-2 Type II scope expansion to cover the agent registry + audit ledger — combined with the May 7 CISA KEV-catalog addition of n8n CVE-2026-21858 (Ni8mare), the same-day LangChain LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 SSRF (CVSS 9.1) + LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188 auth-bypass (CVSS 8.8) disclosure pair, the +34%/4-week MCP-server exposure compounding (~9,400 internet-exposed servers, ~58% with no authorization controls), and the May 7 Microsoft Defender for Cloud MCP-server threat-detection module GA forces enterprise procurement RFPs to name a signed-skill registry + per-tenant capability gating + per-org audit-ledger triple as a baseline requirement for any agentic-AI orchestrator entering the enterprise tier. The forcing function is that the dual-registry shape now spans both major frontier labs and is reinforced by hyperscaler-side telemetry (Defender XDR for MCP) within the same disclosure window — enterprise CISOs and procurement teams adopt the registry-first posture as the operational answer to the n8n KEV catalog + LangGraph/LiteLLM CVE pair. The shape is most likely an explicit RFP control family naming sandboxed-skill registry + per-tenant Mythos-class capability gating + per-org audit ledger, not a generic "AI governance" line item. Hyperscaler-managed registry tiers (Microsoft Foundry / AWS Bedrock / Google Vertex) ship parallel offerings within the same window to avoid being the lone hold-out without a contractual control plane.

reasoning.because: Anthropic + OpenAI both shipped signed agent-skill / per-org agent registries on May 7.
reasoning.given: n8n Ni8mare KEV add + LangGraph SSRF + LiteLLM auth-bypass force agentic-platform governance.
reasoning.so_that: Enterprise procurement RFPs name signed-skill registry + per-tenant gating as baseline for agentic orchestrators.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; >=1 hyperscaler-managed registry tier ships in parallel.
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic and OpenAI both launched signed agent registries the same day; soon enterprise buyers will require them in contracts.

predictions.summary: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 ships a sandboxed-skill registry + per-tenant Mythos gating same day OpenAI launches a per-org agent registry with FedRAMP-Moderate authorization. By Q4 2026 enterprise RFPs name signed-skill registry + per-tenant capability gating as baseline for agentic-AI orchestrators.
